_header: Extra header fields after the four fixed integers (magic, version, format digest, kernel schema, compiler identity), in declaration order. `string` is length-prefixed UTF-8. `app_id` is the app identity, reverse-DNS: bake writes it from DataSource::app_id(); empty is unnamed (a fixture or a stand-in) and unnamed matches anything at boot. `router` names the root slot filled before initializers.

header.name: locale
header._comment: The root string slot holding the resolved locale every `t(...)` reads; set only when the app calls `t`. The runner writes it from set_place.

header.name: snapshot_entry
header._comment: Empty for a running app, otherwise the snapshot entry kind; checked before decoding tables.

header.name: snapshot_refresh
header._comment: The snapshot refresh signature, number -> {date: number, props: Props}[]. Absent on a running app.

_about: The single declaration authority for the plan: its tables, the expression VM's opcodes, the stdlib roster, and the enum vocabularies. plan/build.rs generates the row structs, the canonical encoder, the validating decoder, the opcode and stdlib enums, and FORMAT_DIGEST from this file. Nothing here is hand-mirrored anywhere else. Kernel node types, props, and style rows are NOT declared here: plan rows carry the kernel's ordinals as numbers, and the crates that give them meaning take the vocabulary from exact-kernel.
_codecs: u8 | u16 | u32 | i32 | f64 | bool | str (u32 index into the string pool) | enum:<Name> (u8 ordinal) | idx:<table> (u32 row index, validated) | opt:<table> (u32 row index or NONE = 0xFFFFFFFF) | range:<table> (u32 start + u32 len, validated) | code (u32 offset + u32 len into the code pool, validated as well-formed bytecode) | bytes (u32 offset + u32 len into the data pool)
_tables: Document order is significant: nodes and regions with the same parent are ordered by `order`; an arm's content is every node and region whose `arm` names it; a node with no parent inside an arm is one of the arm's roots. A font face is one source path, a weight range (`weight` to `weight_max`; one weight is both), a stretch range in tenths of a percent (`stretch_min` to `stretch_max`; 1000 is normal width) and an italic flag, as an `@font-face` rule's descriptors. The compiler reads a range the declaration leaves unsaid from the file's `fvar` axes; a host never infers one.

fields.name: owner
fields._comment: The arm whose instance owns this slot — a `for` row, an `if` or `match` arm. The slot is created, its init evaluated in that arm's frames, when the arm instance is created, and dropped with it. None: a root slot.

fields.name: late
fields._comment: A root slot holding the state of a child used outside every region; its init runs once at the boot render, after boot settlement (so it may read derives and resources), not with the other root slots before it. Always false when owner is set.

fields.name: persist
fields._comment: A root slot the host keeps across launches. Boot takes the store's value under `exact.state.<name>` where it decodes to the slot's type (else the initializer's value stands, and the mismatch is journaled); after every commit that stands the store holds the slot's value. Only a root slot (no owner, not late) of a number, string or bool, or an option or list of those.

fields.name: context
fields._comment: Trailing request-context argument count; 0 without `with`. Only persisted kept-answer admission compares the identifying prefix. All live requests, compiled values, carry and document checkpoints compare every argument. Must not exceed args.len.

fields.name: placeholder
fields._comment: The row whose value shows while this one's source hasn't answered and nothing is kept for its arguments — a declared `else source(args)`, compiled as a row of its own (named `<name>#else`, arguments that read no state, the same type, no placeholder of its own). None: a list or an option shows its empty value, and anything else has none.

fields.name: placeholder_value
fields._comment: A declared `else empty(field=value, …)`, the compiler's constant (a value), shown while nothing is kept and the source has not answered. Empty bytes: none — an undeclared placeholder is the type's zero, which the runner computes.

fields.name: refreshes
fields._comment: The resources a send to this mutation refreshes, forced, when it runs and when its reply lands (`mutation m as shape T refreshes a, b`).

fields.name: then
fields._comment: The action a `mutation … then action` runs after each answer lands, as its own commit. None: nothing runs.

fields.name: queue
fields._comment: `mutation m as shape T queue` — one send in flight; a later send waits, with its send-time arguments, until the one before it is answered or let go and its `then` has run. False: the newest send wins.

tables.name: modules
tables._comment: The sources that are a native module's names, which the runner routes to the native slot rather than the app's data. `declared` and `extension` are what the wire carries; `request` is `always`, `when-prompt` or `never`; `sync` is the synchronous form's name, or empty; `substitute` is what the agent's runner answers with no implementation bound, a JSON object.

tables.name: module_events
tables._comment: A native module's event the app's root hears, and the action it runs with the event's arguments, as many as the action takes. `raised` is `activation` (a person's act on the platform's UI, which only the host raises), `emit` (the device's) or `wake` (the host's alone, at the platform's call, each an invocation of a wake); `hold` bounds the deliveries held before the session can hear them; `budget` is a wake event's milliseconds from the wake's first delivery to its deadline, 0 for any other.

tables.name: tools
tables._comment: A root action offered to a caller that is not the person. `consequence` is `reads`, `writes` or `destroys`; `returns`, `fails` and `available` are the derives holding the line's clauses; `face` is the manifest's `intents` face for it as a JSON object, or empty for a tool with none.

fields.name: name
fields._comment: The task's name, for the agent's `state.tasks`.

fields.name: gated
fields._comment: `task t when cond`: the timer is armed while `gate` is true and idle (an infinite deadline) while it is false. False: `mount`, armed from boot.

fields.name: gate
fields._comment: The gate, a bool, evaluated at each commit after its settlement; the constant `true` for an ungated task.

fields.name: keyed
fields._comment: `key=expr`: a changed key (compared as a `for` key is) re-arms the timer from the commit's time.

fields.name: key
fields._comment: The key, a string, number or bool; the constant `true` when not keyed.

tables.name: sequences
tables._comment: Each `sequence NAME when gate key=key` and its `play(tracks, bpm=, from=, countIn=, clock=, clockOut=, ended=)`. The gate and key are a task's; the arguments are plan code the runner evaluates after each commit's settlement and compares by value. An omitted argument is a constant: `from` 0, `countIn` [], `clock` and `clockOut` "".

tables.name: activity_slots
tables._comment: Independent placement roots in one snapshot session; no refresh. Names are lockScreen, compactLeading, compactTrailing, minimal, expanded.leading, expanded.trailing, expanded.center and expanded.bottom.

fields.name: written
fields._comment: Whether the author wrote this row on this node: an attribute of the node, or a row of a `style` its `class` names. False for a row the compiler implies (a tag's fixed row, a heading's size and weight, a link run's colour, a sheet's rows, a row derived from another). Set where lowering emits the row; where two rows set one property, the winner's. The runner hands a style row's to the kernel, which keeps it beside the row (`StyleProps::written`); a prop row's is carried and read by nothing yet.

tables.name: looks
tables._comment: A `:hover` or `:focus-visible` look on a node `node` (rows in node order, at most one a state a node; a node with none has no row, so a plan without state parts pays nothing), which the host applies on its own tracking with no round trip: `state` 1 `:hover`, 2 `:focus-visible` (0, once `:active`, is retired and refused: `:active` lowers to the press paint); `bindings` its style rows, each a literal (a token's name is one, as a static row's): `background-color`, a side's `border-*-color`, `opacity`, `box-shadow`. A host composes them over the base, `:hover` then `:focus-visible`, under the press paint; a disabled node takes none.

fields.name: render
fields._comment: When the route's document renders; undeclared is client.

fields.name: activate
fields._comment: When a rendered page's runtime loads; inferred when undeclared.

fields.name: paint
fields._comment: What a served page's reader sees first; `settled` (undeclared) is the settled page, `boot` the boot document, sent before any answer, then the settled page.

fields.name: pages
fields._comment: The source that lists a parameterized route's pages — the values of its one parameter, a list<string> — for the build to render and the server's sitemap to name. Empty: none.

fields.name: pages_args
fields._comment: That source's arguments, values (a list in the plan's value encoding); empty bytes without a source.

tables.name: keyframes
tables._comment: The app's `@keyframes` rules by name, each body as CSS text (`0%{r:3px;}100%{r:9px;}`); the runner resolves `animation-name` against them.

tables.name: sounds
tables._comment: Each declared sound, a WAV the compiler read: its app-relative path (what `playSound` names), its length in frames at its own rate, its channels, and the SHA-256 of its bytes as hex. The runner reads a voice's natural length, frames / rate; the hosts read which files to decode.

tables.name: profiles
tables._comment: The app's `@color-profile`s by name: the ICC file (an asset path) and the rendering intent; `color(--name …)` resolves against them, and the platform draws it.

tables.name: theme
tables._comment: The app's `theme`, one row an entry: its name, the role it overrides as a row writes it (`-exact-secondary-label`, `Canvas`; empty for none), the text it stands for, which names no entry, and its kind. A string row naming an entry of its kind or an overridden role reads that text, in the compiler and when the runner sets a row.

fields.name: kind
fields._comment: The token's kind, which rows may name it: 0 a colour, 1 a length (px text, one `rem` or `em`, or a named length), 2 a number, 3 a `box-shadow`, 4 a `text-shadow` (the row's own text, its colours folded). A string row reads an entry of its row's kind; `value` and the slices are its text in that kind.

fields.name: slices
fields._comment: A token that varies by an app axis has one slice per full app tuple, in tuple order (mixed radix over `axes`, the first axis most significant); `value` is the default tuple's. Empty for a token that does not vary.

tables.name: theme_slices
tables._comment: One token's text for one full app tuple; a `theme` row's `slices` range names its own.

tables.name: axes
tables._comment: The app's axes in declaration order, each with its values joined by `|`, the first the default. `-exact-mode` pins a node's value per axis; the window's are `setMode`'s.

tables.name: icons
tables._comment: Each icon token the plan keeps, which a computed `symbol:` source may name (`symbol:icon.reply`, or `symbol:sf/<name>` for the icon whose `sf` it is): its SF Symbol (empty for none), the SVG's viewBox and its paths' `d` joined by `;`, drawn as a template as a role's path is (empty for a file the web draws as written), and the SVG's path under `assets/` (empty for none). A literal source is written at build as `symbol:icon|<sf>|<view_box>|<path>|<svg>`, the image source form hosts read (`exact_kernel::Icon`): `<path>` is each SVG path's `d` joined by `;`, each filled nonzero; no part holds a `|`, which the build refuses.

tables.name: hatches
tables._comment: Each hatch word app.json declares, with the platforms whose module handles it as a mask (bit 0 ios, 1 tvos, 2 macos, 3 web, 4 linux, 5 windows, 6 android; a plain list is every bit). A host calls a word only where its bit is set, so a platform taken off a word stops being called with the next bundle.

tables.name: views
tables._comment: Each custom-element tag the app's views place that a package serves rather than the app's own module, with the extension whose implementation makes it in each session. `displayed`: the runner reports each instance's displayed state to that implementation, with the origin of the commit that changed it; `binds`: the props, by name separated by spaces, whose changes it reports the same way.

tables.name: texts
tables._comment: One localized text, `{name}` placeholders unfilled. Within a locale, sorted by key.

tables.name: locales
tables._comment: One strings table per locale (BCP 47 name). Row 0 is the base; the rest are in name order. rtl is the CLDR script direction, compiled once. Table names remain for data-only strings. Only the keys the app's `t` calls name.

_enums: Wire ordinal is the 0-based index. An unknown ordinal is a typed decode rejection.
_opcodes: The expression VM: a stack machine over values with a small locals stack (`BindLocal` pops into it, `LoadLocal` copies from it, `DropLocal` pops it) for names an inline `match` binds and the item and index a `Map`/`Filter` callback binds. Each opcode names its operand layout; the decoder validates framing and every index operand. `depth` operands count enclosing instance scopes (0 = innermost). Type inference guarantees stack discipline; the VM still traps, never UB.

opcodes.name: LoadIndex
opcodes._comment: The position (a number from 0) of the `for` row `depth` scopes out, as `for item, i in list` names it.

opcodes.name: Map
opcodes._comment: Pops a list; runs the callback body that follows inline up to the operand's offset once per item, with the item and its index bound as the next two locals; pushes the list of the values the body leaves.

opcodes.name: Filter
opcodes._comment: As `Map`, keeping each item whose body leaves `true`.

opcodes.name: FailureResource
opcodes._comment: `failure(x)`: once the resource settled, `none` while its latest request for its current arguments has not failed, else `some` of the compiler's `Failure` record, `{ code, message }` by position.

_stdlib: The enumerated roster: every callable an expression may name, with its parameter types and return type (`any` = one of number, string, bool, list). The compiler checks calls against this table; the runner's VM implements each entry once; entries are added by fixture, never by speculation. Router and Entry name reserved record shapes; list<Router>, list<Entry>, and list<string> are typed lists.

stdlib.name: performanceNow
stdlib._comment: The web's `performance.now()`: milliseconds on the runner's monotonic clock since boot (the driver's clock under the agent, from 0), not the date. Renamed from `now()`, which is refused (`type-now-renamed`).

stdlib.name: formatTime
stdlib._comment: `h:mm AM` of (epochMs, utcOffset minutes east), as Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: <the offset>, timeStyle: "short" }) prints it. Core: every app links it, as it linked formatClockTime. A parameter spelled as string literals (`"a" | "b"`) is a string the compiler requires written as one of them.

stdlib.name: includes
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.includes(needle)`: a case-sensitive literal substring search; the empty needle matches. Over a list of strings, numbers or bools, `Array.prototype.includes(item)` (SameValueZero: NaN is NaN, -0 is 0), one list step per item scanned up to the match. `any` is the type checker's. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: trim
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's String.prototype.trim — ECMA-262 WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, not Rust's White_Space.

stdlib.name: first
stdlib._comment: A list's first item, `some(x)`, or `none` for an empty list; `any` is `list<T>` in and `option<T>` out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: t
stdlib._comment: The text for (locale, key), placeholders filled from name/value pairs. The compiler writes every argument; an author writes `t("key", name=value)`.

stdlib.name: map
stdlib._comment: `map(list<T>, (T, number) => U) -> list<U>` (the type checker's). Lowered to the `Map` opcode, never `Call`: the row reserves the name.

stdlib.name: filter
stdlib._comment: `filter(list<T>, (T, number) => bool) -> list<T>`. Lowered to the `Filter` opcode, never `Call`.

stdlib.name: join
stdlib._comment: The web's `Array.prototype.join` over a list of strings, numbers or bools, each printed as `toString` prints it.

stdlib.name: formatDate
stdlib._comment: The calendar date of (epochMs, utcOffset), as Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") prints it: `medium` is { dateStyle: "medium" }, `month-year` is { month: "long", year: "numeric" }. `iso` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, the date at that wall time: `Date.prototype.toISOString`'s date part at a whole-minute offset (a fractional offset's wall time is not clipped to a millisecond again, as no style's is); outside years 1–9999 it prints `""`, as every style does. The linked capability `format`.

stdlib.name: formatNumber
stdlib._comment: `compact` is Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { notation: "compact", roundingMode: "trunc", signDisplay: "negative" }). `decimal` is Intl.NumberFormat("en-US") (grouped, at most three fraction digits), `currency` with an ISO 4217 code { style: "currency", currency } (`$1,481.47`, `-$5.00`, the code's own fraction digits), `percent` { style: "percent" } (`26%`): each rounds the value's shortest decimal digits half away from zero, as ICU does, and signs a negative zero. The code is written only with `currency`, and the compiler fills `""` for a call that omits it. Every style prints `""` for a non-finite value. The linked capability `format`.

stdlib.name: frame
stdlib._comment: Where layout put the first node whose `id` prop is the argument, as last laid out: its border box in its root's space, free of transforms and scrolling. Actions only (the compiler refuses it elsewhere).

stdlib.name: measure
stdlib._comment: The node's border box as if its `height` were `auto`, under the offer it has now. Actions only; the id is a string literal, so the runner answers it before the action runs.

stdlib.name: at
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's Array.prototype.at — `some` of the item at an index truncated toward zero, counted from the end when negative, `none` past either end; `any` is `list<T>` in and `option<T>` out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: startsWith
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.startsWith(prefix)`: whether the text begins with the prefix, case-sensitive; the empty prefix matches. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: endsWith
stdlib._comment: The web's `String.prototype.endsWith(suffix)`: whether the text ends with the suffix, case-sensitive; the empty suffix matches. The web's optional end-position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: slice
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.slice(start, end?)` over UTF-16 code units (ToIntegerOrInfinity: NaN is 0, fractions truncate, a negative index counts from the end, both clamped); an omitted `end` is `Number.MAX_VALUE`, which clamps as `undefined` does (a plan's constants are finite, so not `Infinity`). The result is made well formed: a lone surrogate half becomes U+FFFD. Over a list, `Array.prototype.slice(start, end?)` by the same clamp, one list step per item kept, the result's extent checked as a `List` is; `any` is `string` or `list<T>` in and the same out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: replaceAll
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.replaceAll(find, with)` with a string `find`: every match, left to right, `GetSubstitution` applied (`$$`, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`; `$1` is literal), an empty `find` inserting at every code-unit boundary; the whole result made well formed once, and bounded by `MAX_STRING` UTF-8 bytes as it is built.

stdlib.name: toLowerCase
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.toLowerCase()`: Unicode's default, locale-independent mapping with final sigma. Linked by use: it reaches the kernel's case tables through `text-transform`'s link (capability `text_transform`), bounded by `MAX_STRING`.

stdlib.name: concat
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Array.prototype.concat(other)` of two lists of one item type, `list<T>, list<T> -> list<T>` (the type checker's): one list step per item of the result, taken before it is built, then its extent checked as a `List` is.

stdlib.name: indexOf
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.indexOf(needle)` — the first match's position in UTF-16 code units, `-1` for none, 0 for the empty needle — or, over a list of strings, numbers or bools, `Array.prototype.indexOf(item)` by IsStrictlyEqual (NaN is never found, -0 is 0), one list step per item scanned up to the match. `any` is the type checker's. The web's optional position argument is not taken.

stdlib.name: split
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.split(separator)` with a string separator: the pieces between its matches, left to right; an empty separator splits into UTF-16 code units (each piece made well formed: a lone half is U+FFFD), and `""` into no pieces. One list step per piece, taken before the list is built, then its extent checked as a `List` is. The web's limit argument and regular expressions are not taken.

stdlib.name: elementFromPoint
stdlib._comment: DOM's `document.elementFromPoint(x, y)?.closest("[id]")?.id` over `frame`'s boxes: the `id` of the front-most laid-out box at the viewport point (every scroll and transform applied; ancestors' overflow clips; `pointer-events: none`, `display: none` and `visibility: hidden` skipped; the kernel's paint order), or of its nearest ancestor with one; `none` where no box or ancestor has one. Actions only.

stdlib.name: elementsFromPoint
stdlib._comment: Action-only point read; own nonempty ids of every hit node, including hit ancestors, front to back, with elementFromPoint's skips and transforms.

stdlib.name: querySelectorAll
stdlib._comment: Action-only structural read. Only [data-<declared word>~="value"] is accepted; own ids of mounted, displayed, non-inert matches in tree order.

stdlib.name: parseNumber
stdlib._comment: A decimal number in text, `some(n)`, else `none`. Surrounding whitespace is `trim`'s; then an optional sign, digits with an optional fraction or a fraction alone (`.5`; `5.` is 5), and an optional decimal exponent (`1e3`); nothing else (`""`, hex, `Infinity`, `NaN`, `12px` are `none`). The value is the correctly rounded double, as `Number()` reads it; a result past the largest finite is `none`, as is a nonzero numeral that rounds to zero; `-0` is -0.

stdlib.name: ceil
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Math.ceil`, IEEE's ceiling (`ceil(-0.5)` is -0; NaN and the infinities are their own).

stdlib.name: round
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Math.round`: the nearest integer, a tie toward +∞ (`round(-1.5)` is -1, `round(2.5)` is 3), and -0 for a negative input that rounds to zero (`round(-0.4)` is -0); NaN and the infinities are their own. Not Rust's `f64::round`, which breaks a tie away from zero.

stdlib.name: calendarDiff
stdlib._comment: The whole calendar years or months from the first ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, proleptic Gregorian, years 0 through 9999) to the second, counted as an age is: a period completes when the later date's month and day reach the earlier date's (years compare month then day, months compare the day), so a Feb 29 start completes a year on Mar 1 of a common year and a Jan 31 start completes a month on Mar 1, as the web's `Temporal.PlainDate.prototype.until` counts with `largestUnit` `"years"` or `"months"` (date-fns' `differenceInMonths` differs: it lets a month's last day complete a month). When the second date is earlier, the count from it to the first, negated. `none` when either is not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` date.

stdlib.name: toFixed
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Number.prototype.toFixed(digits)`, the binary value rounded (`toFixed(1.005, 2)` is `"1.00"`, a tie away from zero on the exact value), `-0.001` at 2 is `"-0.00"`, a magnitude of `1e21` or more printed as `toString` prints it. One declared difference: a non-finite number prints `""`, where JavaScript prints `NaN` or `Infinity`. `digits` is a whole-number literal from 0 to 100, JavaScript's range. A linked `format` entry.

stdlib.name: formatDecimal
stdlib._comment: An integer count of a smallest unit as a decimal with `digits` places, exactly (`formatDecimal(1234, 2)` is `"12.34"`, `formatDecimal(-5, 2)` is `"-0.05"`, `formatDecimal(7, 0)` is `"7"`); `-0` prints as `0`. A count that is not an integer, or not finite, prints `""`: money is a count of cents, or `formatDecimal(round(price * 100), 2)` for a price of at most two decimals under a trillion. `digits` is a whole-number literal from 0 to 20. A linked `format` entry.

stdlib.name: formatDay
stdlib._comment: A day's label for (thenMs, nowMs, utcOffset), en-US. The days are the offset's calendar days, as `formatDate`'s are (one fixed offset for both instants: a DST change between them is not applied). `day` is `Today`, `Yesterday` or `Tomorrow`, else `formatDate`'s `medium`; `day-time` adds ` at ` and `formatTime`'s `short` (`Today at 4:42 PM`, `Oct 11, 2026 at 4:42 PM`); `list` is Mail's and Notes' list label: `formatTime`'s `short` today, `Yesterday`, the weekday's name two to six days back, else the numeric short date of Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short" }) (`10/11/26`), a later day's included. `""` when either instant is invalid as `formatDate` judges one. Pure: the app passes its own `now`. The linked capability `format`.

stdlib.name: sin
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Math.sin` and CSS's `sin()`, of radians. The native runners compute it with `libm` (`exact_motion::math`), the same bits on every target; the web's JS target is `Math.sin`, which ECMA-262 lets differ in the last bits. NaN and the infinities are NaN.

stdlib.name: cos
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Math.cos` and CSS's `cos()`, of radians, computed as `sin` is.

stdlib.name: sum
stdlib._comment: A list of numbers added left to right from +0, exactly `xs.reduce((a, x) => a + x, 0)`: `[]` is 0, `[-0]` is +0, a NaN or opposite infinities make NaN. A step an item on the evaluation's list budget, as `includes` takes. Not `Math.sumPrecise`, which rounds once.

stdlib.name: sortBy
stdlib._comment: `sortBy(list<T>, (T, number) => K, "asc" | "desc"?) -> list<T>` with `K` a number or a string (the type checker's). Lowered as the list bound once as a local, a `Map` of the key callback over it (one list step an item, the key evaluated once an item), then this call on (the list, its keys, descending): the items in a stable order of their keys, a bottom-up merge sort written out alike in the runner and the JS target. Numbers by `<` with NaN as +0 (so -0, +0 and NaN tie); strings by UTF-16 code units, as `<`; equal keys keep their input order in both directions. The call takes no list step: its n·⌈log₂ n⌉ comparisons are the stated cost; the list it builds is measured as `List` measures one.

stdlib.name: toUpperCase
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `String.prototype.toUpperCase()`: Unicode's default, locale-independent full mapping, expansions included (`ß` is `SS`). Linked by use through the same case tables as `toLowerCase` (capability `text_transform`), bounded by `MAX_STRING`. Displayed text is uppercased by `text-transform`, not by this.

stdlib.name: range
stdlib._comment: Exact's own, not the web's: the whole numbers 0 to n - 1 in order, `[]` for 0. `n` is a whole number at least 0 (`-0` is 0); any other, NaN and the infinities included, is a `TypeMismatch` trap, as the arguments do not fit (the compiler refuses such a literal). One list step an item, taken before the list is built (as `concat`), so an `n` past the bound traps `IterationLimit`; the list's extent is checked as a `List` is.

stdlib.name: flat
stdlib._comment: JavaScript's `Array.prototype.flat()` at its default depth, 1: a list of lists' items in order, `list<list<T>> -> list<T>` (the type checker's; no depth is taken). One list step an outer item and one an item it emits, taken before the list is built, as `concat` takes them; the result's extent is checked as a `List` is.

stdlib.name: rangeFrame
stdlib._comment: `Range.getBoundingClientRect()` of a text field's UTF-16 range, read in an action from the field's last presented layout: offsets truncated toward zero; a collapsed range the caret's rectangle, a wider one the union of its line fragments, untrimmed by scrolling or the field's clip. Unavailable for a non-finite or negative offset, a start past the end, an end past the text, a missing or hidden field, active composition, or a host with no reader.

stdlib.name: sharedFiles
stdlib._comment: The files a received share carried, by the token in the entry's `name` parameter: `{files: Picked[], dropped, pending}`, `pending` those still being copied. A token the host did not set this launch answers no files. The host sets the token by `set_shared`, so a read is not a pure function of its arguments: the runner re-evaluates its readers at every update.

stdlib.name: fragment
stdlib._comment: The entry's fragment, what its location had after `#` with the fragment percent-encode set applied, `""` when none. It is no part of the screen's identity; a host scrolls to the element it names once the route's content has arrived.

_sources: The data seam's signatures. One row per data-source name the app's `resource` and `send` declarations use, with the parameter types and the result type every use agrees on (the compiler refuses a disagreement by name). An executor that marshals by shape — the TypeScript module's — reads this table at bind; a Rust crate ignores it. formatVersion 3.
_resources: `reader` (formatVersion 4): the bake found this resource consulting the store. Its `initial` is then the empty-store answer — the fresh install's first frame, never a developer's session (the bake's store is empty by construction) — and the runner treats it as a placeholder: a kept answer from the device's store beats it, and a data source that is not ready at boot (a TypeScript module before its host loads it) is asked again at `data_ready`. `initial_args` is a canonical Value::List of evaluated bake arguments, empty bytes only without a compiled value; initial is reused only for equal arguments. `context` is the trailing request-context count (0 without `with`), bounded by args.len. The persisted kept entry stores only the identifying prefix; only its admission while the source is unready compares that prefix. Every live request, compiled value, carry and document checkpoint still compares the full arguments.
